decisive_difference: All three give the same top-line answer (two records, not one) and none proposes an illegal property or a class that fails its own scope note. B is clearly last: it never unfolds P1 into E15 (the case is precisely about who assigned what, when -- prose that types no event), carries an unused E41 in classes_proposed, and its own notes admit its supporting citation is an analogy rather than a direct precedent. A and C are extremely close and share almost the entire model; C edges ahead only because it models the shared numbering book (E29, verified against Issue 159's outcome) as a direct response to a fact stated in the case, where A's comparably strong unique find (Issue 383's Sanderson/Doerr exchange, the single most on-point precedent among all three answers for duplicated-string identity) supports a secondary aside A itself says doesn't change the answer either way.
notes: A vs C is genuinely close and could plausibly reorder on a re-read -- both are excellent, near-identical in mechanism, and each found a real, verified citation the other missed (A: Issue 383; C: Issue 159/E29).
